title: Law School introduces largely permissive AI policy
snippet: Columbia Law School introduced a permissive generative AI policy allowing students to use AI as a 'learning aid' (e.g., studying legal concepts, generating hypotheticals, summarizing cases) while continuing to bar its use to generate submitted content.
match_reason: websearch (news_article) — This precedent-setting policy at a peer R1 law school directly contrasts with UC Berkeley Law's restrictive AI ban, providing critical sector-wide context for the UC AI Steering Committee.

title: ORI's Guidance on Generative Artificial Intelligence Released
snippet: The U.S. Office of Research Integrity (ORI) released new guidance for institutions navigating research misconduct proceedings involving generative AI. The guidance covers identifying accepted practices, proving misconduct beyond AI detectors, and disclosing AI use in papers and grant applications.
match_reason: websearch (position_statement) — This federal guidance directly impacts research-security and integrity standards for all PHS-funded research institutions, including the entire University of California system.
